scout.d: +1 damage to friendlies in the four adjacent cells. Carries no weapon.

recon.d: Calls in two more cards, then is gone. Leaves no unit on the board.

pathfinder.d: On deployment, claims the two tiles ahead as your ground.

vanguard.d: +3 damage while at full hull. Loses it the moment it takes a scratch.

rifle.d: Fires down its lane every turn. No special behaviour.

ab.d: Heal every adjacent personnel unit for 4 instead of the unit ahead.

medic.d: Heals every friendly in the four adjacent cells each turn. Carries no weapon.

archer.d: Covers its own flanks while firing forward.

assassin.d: Deploys on any tile, including hostile ground. Fragile once it lands.

samurai.d: Cuts every cell around it, including behind.

marks.d: Ignores everything in front and hits the furthest hostile in the lane.

lancer.d: Strikes all three cells ahead at once.

mortar.d: Indirect fire. Cannot hit anything closer than its blast.

ab.d: Shield holds against two attacks this turn instead of one.

bulwark.d: A one-cell shield that is itself the wall. Absorbs one attack per turn, then regenerates.

ronin.d: Cuts ahead and behind in the same motion.

naginata.d: Polearm reach — it strikes the second cell as readily as the first.

kunoichi.d: Deploys on any tile. Blind to whatever stands directly beside her.

herald.d: +1 damage to every friendly in the same lane.

wall.d: No weapon, no shield, no legs. Blocks the lane in both directions.

supply.d: Drops a munitions pallet on landing: +2 deploy points immediately.

beacon.d: Claims the three cells ahead of it the moment it lands.

cache.d: +3 deploy points this turn. The scramble costs you a card at random from your hand.

shield.d: Attach to a unit. Absorbs the next incoming attack entirely, then breaks.

relay.d: +1 damage to every friendly in its column, across all five lanes.

techblade.d: Hits across lanes without leaving its own.

pulse.d: Anchored resonator. Pulses every surrounding cell each turn.

scrambler.d: Every hostile in its lane deals 1 less damage. Does not stack with itself.

battery.d: Anchored particle lance. Direct fire — a blocker of yours cuts the beam.

knight.d: Blocks the lane, regenerates its shield, and ripostes against anything that strikes it. Personnel — a Medic can patch it, a Tech Medic cannot.

ab.d: Every friendly in this lane gains a shield this turn.

aegis.d: Two cells deep, with regenerating shields. Seals a lane against chip damage.

biomed.d: Applies regeneration to every Common unit in its column, refreshed while it lives.

ab.d: Burst-repair every Tech unit in the column for 8 and restore broken shields.

techmed.d: Trickles repair into Tech in its column, or dumps it all at once on the ability.

ab.d: Vault and strike any hostile exactly two cells away in any direction for 6.

dragoon.d: Thrusters let it leap and strike anything two cells out, in any direction.

railgun.d: Pierces the whole lane, ignoring armour floors.

hell.d: Two pods dropped on any tile, including hostile ground. Each damages on landing.

plasma.d: The plasma lingers two turns, burning anything standing in it and denying capture.

ab.d: Barrel two cells forward. Anything struck takes 8 and is stunned for a turn.

exo.d: Twenty hull and a charge that shatters whatever it collides with.

cipher.d: Trades places with any friendly unit on the board. Uses its action for the turn.

engineer.d: No weapon. The Tech unit directly ahead hits harder and repairs every turn.

outrider.d: Charges two cells. Whatever it strikes is driven back a cell.

fob.d: Deploys on held ground, in columns three and beyond. Adjacent friendlies repair and cool down faster. Immobile.

mine.d: Damages the first hostile that enters, then spent. Visible — hostiles route around it when they can.

hecate.d: Reaches any lane on the board. Needs a turn to cycle — it cannot fire twice running.

dynamo.d: +1 deploy point at the start of each turn while it stands, stacking to +2. No weapon.

pikewall.d: Braced spears that hold the ground they strike.

sentry.d: Answers twice as hard as it is struck.

falconer.d: Calls in one more card on deployment, and still carries a rifle.

rampart.d: Nine hull and one gun. Holds a lane without shielding it.

piercer.d: Anchored railspike. Armour floors mean nothing to it; a blocker of yours still cuts the beam.

suppressor.d: Every hostile in its lane deals 2 less damage.

reactor.d: A bigger pallet than the Supply Drone, on a thinner hull.

bore.d: Anchored and armour-piercing. Ignores what a floor was supposed to stop.

kessen.d: Deploys on any tile, including hostile ground.

ram.d: Charges, then holds the ground it takes instead of riding through it.

marshal.d: Buffs its lane and its column at once.

longshot.d: Reaches the furthest hostile in the lane, through anything in the way.

sapper.d: Deploys on any tile, including hostile ground. Opens up on whatever is ahead of where it lands.

rearguard.d: Faces the wrong way on purpose. Strikes behind it at any range — the only ranged answer to something already past your line.

backstop.d: One volley across both home columns, every lane at once. Fired once, then spent.

ab.d: Slide one lane toward the heavier side and cut every hostile in the column ahead for 6.

ashura.d: A four-armed war frame. The scythes sweep the column ahead across three lanes at once, so nothing gets past it by stepping sideways.

pilot.d: Carries no weapon and cannot hold a cell. Deploy one, keep it alive, and a Frame can land on it — that is the whole job.

whitedevil.d: The all-rounder. A regenerating shield and a service blade that cuts everything at contact — all four sides at once. Five prototype weapons re-spec it to whatever the mission is.

sevenblades.d: The melee frame. One swing of the arm blade takes the column ahead across all three lanes — it does not want range, it wants to be standing where you put it.

heavyarms.d: The artillery frame. Anchored, heaviest hull on the field, and a ballistic gatling that walks fire three cells down the lane.

servo.d: May move AND fire in the same turn.

coolant.d: Ability cooldowns are 1 turn shorter, minimum 1.

phase.d: The first killing blow leaves it at 1 hull instead. Once per deployment.

weave.d: +1 shield capacity. Stacks with regenerating shields.

dropod.d: May deploy straight onto a hostile below Specialist tier, crushing it on landing and holding the cell.

stim.d: +2 damage. The unit loses 1 hull every turn it lives.

ifield.d: Immune to indirect fire — Mortar, Plasma Artillerist, anything that arcs.

twinlink.d: May move AND fire in the same turn. +1 damage.

adaptive.d: +4 hull. +1 shield capacity, stacks with regenerating shields.

overclock.d: Ignores hostile armour floors. Ability cooldowns are 1 turn shorter, minimum 1.

ghostplate.d: The first killing blow leaves it at 1 hull instead, once per deployment. +1 shield capacity.

rapidkit.d: Costs 1 less deploy point, minimum 1. May move AND fire in the same turn.

opticsrelay.d: Direct fire ignores blockers in the lane — reaches whatever the weapon would otherwise be denied.

rearsights.d: Also strikes the cell directly behind this unit. Nothing flanks it.

cannon.d: Fires a second time every turn, at the same targets.

greatsword.d: Replaces the Seven Blades' arm blade. One swing takes the whole area directly ahead.

longsword.d: Replaces the Seven Blades' arm blade. Reach — it strikes at three cells without ever closing.

lasergat.d: Replaces the Heavy Arms gatling. Both forward diagonals at once, and nothing at all in the centre.

missilegat.d: Replaces the Heavy Arms gatling. A cross of warheads centred three cells out.

beamrifle.d: The standard barrel. One hostile down the lane, hit very hard.

beamsaber.d: Brutal at contact, and it answers anything that strikes the frame.

javelin.d: A two-cell thrust. Reach without giving up the contact fight.

napalm.d: A cone of burning promethium, and the ground keeps burning after it lands.

railcannon.d: Anti-armour. Punches through the front rank to the hostile deepest in the lane, and armour floors do not apply to what it finds there.

crawler.d: Cheap, fast, endless. Floods whatever lane you leave open.
crawler.counter: Nothing clever kills it — just never leave a lane empty.

breacher.counter: Punishes Barricade and Turret spam. Mix personnel into a Tech-heavy line.

spitter.d: Halts at column four and fires the length of the lane.
spitter.counter: Outranges most of your roster, so it punishes turtling. Reach it with indirect fire, or close the gap before it settles.

burrower.d: Emerges mid-board, behind your front line.
burrower.counter: Punishes over-committing forward. Keep something that can turn around.

hulk.d: Slow and heavy. Reduces all incoming damage by 1.
hulk.counter: Punishes chip damage. Bring one big hit rather than many small ones.

spore.d: Immobile emplacement. Releases a Crawler every two turns and holds its tile until destroyed.
spore.counter: Every turn it lives is another body. Kill it early or drown in them.

pylon.d: Immobile emplacement. +1 damage floor to every hostile in its lane.
pylon.counter: It makes chip damage worthless lane-wide. Armour-piercing ignores it entirely.

jammer.d: Immobile emplacement. Blocks all indirect fire in its lane.
jammer.counter: Shuts off Mortar and Artillerist completely. Only direct fire answers it.

harrower.counter: Barricades and Bulwarks do not stop it. Kill it — do not try to wall it.

chorus.d: Immobile at the far edge. +1 damage to every hostile on the board.
chorus.counter: Kill it first, if you can reach it. Hecate and Longshot can.

sovereign.d: Moves every other turn. Every tile it crosses becomes hostile ground permanently.
sovereign.counter: Ground it takes never comes back. Stop it early, far from your line.

husk.d: Shambles forward and falls apart when destroyed — two Crawlers crawl out of the wreck.
husk.counter: Kill it somewhere you can afford the mess.

mender.d: Carries no weapon. Knits 2 hull back into the most wounded hostile in its lane every turn.
mender.counter: Kill it first, or nothing in that lane stays dead.

screamer.d: Dies loudly. The scream sends every hostile on the board one step forward.
screamer.counter: Time the kill, or the kill times you.

puppeteer.d: Never moves. Every 3 turns it seizes the nearest unit in its lane, turning it against you until it breaks free or the Puppeteer dies.
puppeteer.counter: Keep your best unit out of its lane, or kill it before the third turn lands.

oni.d: A hive-built war frame. It does not queue and it does not wait — it reads your line and walks into whichever lane is thinnest.
oni.counter: It will always be where you are weakest. Hold the lanes evenly, or bring something that cuts across them.

ironbrand.bio: Held the Sundering Gate for nine days with a company of forty. Believes armour is a philosophy.

passive.d: Every unit you deploy arrives with +1 hull.

wildfire.bio: Three commendations, two demotions, one very expensive orbital incident. Fights fast and asks after.

coldwire.bio: Speaks to machines more than people. The machines, notably, keep working.

passive.d: All your units repair 1 hull at the end of every turn.

loneedge.bio: Treats every engagement as a private duel. Plunges into the centre of a formation and trusts the squad to keep up or stay clear.

passive.d: A unit with no friendly in an adjacent cell deals +2 damage.

skunkworks.bio: Ex-skunkworks, permanently caffeinated, trusts machines over orders. Treats the battlefield as a laboratory with inconvenient variables.

passive.d: Tech units deploy with +2 hull and repair 1 hull every turn.

quietstep.bio: Soft-spoken until the unit initialises. Moves through a turn like a rumour and neutralises threats before they resolve.

passive.d: Cards that deploy on hostile ground cost 1 less deploy point, minimum 1.

firebrand.bio: Walked away from a military pedigree to fight at the line. Argues with command, never with her squad.

passive.d: +2 deploy points on any turn after you lost a unit.

riptide.bio: Treats a firefight like a contact sport. No patience for planning, uncanny instinct for where the line is about to break.

passive.d: Units that repositioned this turn take 1 less damage.

stronghold.d: Hold the line through every wave. Each lane's grid charge absorbs one breach — after that, one body through ends it.

civilians.d: A shelter holds the line while survivors run for the edge. Protect it, walk enough of them out, and the block is clear.

specimens.d: Destroy the marked hostile type to fill the quota.

crystals.d: Four crystal nodes on the field. Hold three when the last wave clears.

retake.d: Hold 3 or more tiles in the hostile half when the last wave clears. Bring something that deploys behind their line.

extract.d: Short and heavy. Survive to extraction.

uplink.d: A relay tile sits in contested ground. Hold it three turns in a row to bring the uplink online.

blitz.d: Purge the zone. Destroy nine hostiles before the wave count runs out.

blackout.d: No wave preview and no spawn markers.

crumble.d: Every couple of turns, one open tile collapses for good — impassable to both sides.

ironveil.sub: Delta Shelf · orbital shipyard, no transmission
ironveil.lore:
The Delta Shelf yards built half the fleet holding this sector. Three weeks ago a cluster of small meteors struck the facility. Two weeks later, all transmission went silent.

Command doesn't believe in coincidences.

Secure the facility and salvage the hulls in dock before the structure gives. The yards are worth far more than the rock they sit on — failure to retrieve them is not an option.

say: Commander. We’ve taken an unusual ping off the orbital yards over Zentonia.
Hail went out four hours ago. Nothing came back.
Satellite sweep reads a number of targets moving erratically across the shelf. Origin unknown.
Nothing on the yard registry moves like that. Command advises you enter combat ready — you are weapons free.
beats.reply: Understood. Beachhead first — we take ground, then we take the rest.

say: One more thing, and it came down verbatim. The yards are to be cleared of all hostiles. The yards are of utmost importance.
Do not lose this one, Commander.

intro.close: Channel closed. Descent vector locked — Delta Shelf, Beachhead.

nodes.reqText: Power offline — reset the Power Junction in the Deep Shaft

blackmarrow.lore: The Blackmarrow seams run deeper than any survey admits, and something has been hollowing them out from below. The last crew up sealed the winch station behind them and never said what they saw. The nest is confirmed. Burn it out — and mind the dark below the second gallery, where the power has been out for a month.

say: Commander. Blackmarrow's drill team called it in — their last transmission before they sealed the winch station and pulled everyone topside.
They didn't explain what they saw down there. They just wanted it shut.
Forward team has confirmed nests. Whatever's been hollowing out those lower tunnels has been at it a while.
Note, power's been down at gallery two for a month — central has no eyes past that line. You're going in dark.
beats.reply: Understood. We clear top-down and burn out whatever's holding gallery two.

say: One more thing. Nobody who went past that line came back with a full account of it. Watch your footing, watch each other.
Good hunting, Commander.

intro.close: Channel closed. Descent vector locked — Blackmarrow, Winch Station.

sunderglass.lore: The Sunderglass flats grow the resonant crystal every jump drive in the sector depends on, and the hive grazes on them like cattle. Every day the fields sit contested, the harvest shatters a little more. Cut what can still be saved and get out before the glassing swallows the route home.

say: Commander, Sunderglass is live. Every jump drive in the sector runs on that crystal, and the hive's been grazing the fields for weeks.
Command wants what's left of the harvest before it's gone for good.
beats.reply: Copy. How bad is the shrinkage?

say: Bad, and getting worse by the day. The Shallows are still stable, but Prism Ridge is thinning fast.
Push too far and you hit the Glassing — that's what's left once the hive's done feeding a field. Nothing grows back through it.
beats.reply: Understood. We take what we can hold and pull before the Glassing catches us.

say: One more thing. If the route home starts closing, the crystal isn't worth the wait. Get your people out.
Good hunting, Commander.
beats.reply: Copy. Keep the beer chilled, we'll be home soon.

intro.close: Channel closed. Descent vector locked — Sunderglass, Landing Site.

nodes.lore: The research data lives here. Hold the uplink while it pulls.

nodes.reqText: The research data is still in the spire — secure the Archive Core first

nodes.lore: Survivors barricaded in the dorms. Walking them out is optional — and paid.

lumenspire.lore: Meridian City evacuated in six hours; the Lumenspire research division never made the manifest. Whatever their labs were close to, command wants it badly enough to send a squad back into a dead city for it. The researchers barricaded in the dorms are listed as an optional objective. Their families have been told otherwise.

say: Commander. Meridian evacuated clean six hours ago — except Lumenspire's research division. They never made the manifest.
Whatever they were working on, command wants it enough to send you back into a dead city for it.
beats.reply: Copy. What's the priority — the research, or the people?

say: Officially, the research. The dorms where the barricaded researchers are holed up are listed as an optional objective.
Unofficially — their families were told they were already out. That's not sitting well with me, and it shouldn't sit well with you either.
beats.reply: Understood. We're not leaving anyone we find breathing behind a locked door.

say: That's your call to make down there, Commander, not mine. I just wanted you going in with the full picture.
Good hunting.

intro.close: Channel closed. Descent vector locked — Lumenspire, City Gates.

crownring.sub: Concordat summit · burrowers inside the walls

nodes.lore: The faction reps move on foot. Walk them through the ward.

nodes.reqText: The delegations leave first — clear the Northgate route

crownring.lore: Once a year the Concordat factions meet under one roof to keep the alliance stitched together. This year the burrowers came up through the foundations mid-session — past every checkpoint, straight for the Summit Hall. If the delegations die in the wards, the alliance dies with them and the whole region tips. Walk them out. Whatever it costs.

say: Commander, this one's live right now. The Concordat summit is in session and the burrowers came up through the foundations mid-meeting — every checkpoint bypassed.
They're inside the walls, heading for the Summit Hall.
beats.reply: Copy. What's at stake if we're slow?

say: Every delegation the alliance runs on is sitting in that hall. If they die in the wards, the alliance goes with them, and the whole region tips.
This isn't extraction with extra steps, Commander. Walk them out.
That's the order, verbatim. Command isn't asking for restraint on this one.
Good hunting, Commander.
beats.reply: Copy. Moving to the Summit Hall now.

intro.close: Channel closed. Descent vector locked — Crownring, Summit Hall.

shallowhelm.sub: Fortress Shallow Helm · breached from within

nodes.lore: Restore the couplings. Hold them while they spin up.
The garrison’s last logs. Optional — command pays well for answers.

nodes.reqText: No power on the deck — restore the Power Vault first

nodes.lore: Arm the Purge Protocol and burn out everything it flushes at you.

nodes.reqText: The Purge Protocol isn't armed — fight back to the Purge Core first

shallowhelm.lore: Fortress Shallow Helm anchors the whole defensive line — while it holds, the hive breaks against the pass instead of the cities behind it. Nine days ago, a cult that had spent months quietly worshiping the invaders threw the gates open from the inside, and the wards went dark with them. No distress call went out; there was no one left topside to send one. Arm the Purge Protocol and scour the fortress clean — cultists, hive, and whatever the two have made of each other — then come back out the way you went in.

say: Commander. Shallow Helm is the anchor of the whole line — while it holds, the hive breaks on that pass instead of the cities behind it.
Nine days ago it went dark. No distress call. No survivors on the walls. The gates were sealed from the inside.
beats.reply: Copy. Sealed from the inside — by who?

say: By us, near enough. Command's confirmed a cult inside the garrison — they'd been worshiping the invaders for months and finally opened the gates for them.
The wards didn't fail, Commander. Someone switched them off. The hive's inside now, and so are the people who let them in.
Arm the Purge Protocol and scour that fortress clean — cultists, hive, all of it. Shallow Helm doesn't get to become a hole in the line.
Come back out the way you went in. Good hunting, Commander.

intro.close: Channel closed. Descent vector locked — Shallowhelm, Gatehouse.

targeting.archer: Two ahead plus both rear diagonals
targeting.vert3: Three cells vertically, one column ahead
targeting.bothsides: The cell ahead and the cell behind
targeting.ahead2: Both cells one and two ahead
targeting.rear: Nearest hostile BEHIND it in the lane
targeting.wings: Both forward diagonals — nothing in the centre
targeting.sweep: Every cell in the two columns directly ahead
targeting.cross3: A cross centred three cells ahead
targeting.cone: A flame cone — one cell ahead, then three across

duel.d: One unit gains +4 damage and takes no damage until your next turn.

refit.d: Every Tech unit you control is restored to full hull.

insertion.d: The next three units you deploy this turn may land on any tile, held or not.

breach.d: Destroy every hostile in the chosen column that is at or below 8 hull. Lands at the end of the turn you call it, once the horde has moved.

grapple.d: Drag every hostile in the chosen lane two cells back toward their edge.

requisition.d: +4 deploy points when the call lands.
